core_obligations: Show that a morphism of complexes is a universal quasi-isomorphism iff its image is a quasi-isomorphism, hence S is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulation (proof lines 2428-2436).
Construct the localisation and the canonical comparison functor to D^+(Adeq(O)) (proof lines 2436-2444).
Use the embedding of adequate modules into quasi-coherent sheaves to prove essential surjectivity (proof lines 2446-2455).
Prove the 'fully' part of full faithfulness by rewriting a morphism through a quasi-isomorphism, and state the faithfulness argument (proof lines 2457-2470).
proof_roadmap: Universality of quasi-isomorphisms and the localisation (proof lines 2428-2444).
difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme U = Spec(A), the lemma identifies the bounded below derived category D^+(Adeq(O)) as the localisation of K^+(QCoh(O_U)) at the universal quasi-isomorphisms (statement lines 2419-2426). The proof proceeds in three displayed stages: first it observes that a morphism of complexes of quasi-coherent modules is a universal quasi-isomorphism exactly when its image under the inclusion u is a quasi-isomorphism, so the collection S is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure and the localisation exists with a canonical comparison functor; then it uses that every adequate module embeds in a quasi-coherent sheaf to produce, for a bounded below complex of adequate modules, a quasi-isomorphism from it to the image of a bounded below complex of quasi-coherent modules, giving essential surjectivity; and finally it verifies full faithfulness by replacing an arbitrary zig-zag in the derived category by one in the localisation, and states that faithfulness is proved similarly (proof lines 2428-2470). The level is H3: the identification is carried out through a genuine localisation computation with the two homotopy-category conditions verified.
